32. I honestly believed that this practice was lawful, and for that reason I never attempted to conceal or mislead others as to what I was doing. I used the company name of China Status, and I signed and affixed the company chop on the SDN application forms openly. With even minimal enquiry, it would have been apparent to the authorities that China Status was not the company carrying out the actual works. I acted in this open manner because I did not consider the arrangement to be improper or problematic.

(E) Relationship with Prestige Constructions & Engineering Co. Limited  
(宏業建築工程有限公司)

33. I first came into contact with PC&E when working for my previous employer Marvel Fire Engineering Co. Ltd. While I do not recall the exact year, I remember that it was in the course of a large-scale project. In that project, PC&E was responsible for the building construction works, whereas Marvel Fire Engineering Co. Ltd. was responsible for the fire service systems, installations and equipment.

34. In 2017, I re-established contact with Gordon Ho of PC&E (“Gordon”) as a business acquaintance. Gordon informed me that PC&E would be engaging a RFSIC to carry out improvement works under Fire Safety (Buildings) Ordinance (Cap. 572) in connection with one of PC&E’s projects, and asked me to provide a quotation on behalf of China Status. China Status was eventually engaged by PC&E for this project.

35. After the above, I continued to collaborate with Gordon on other projects. For all instances, Gordon would be the person making the initial telephone call to me, to explain the scope of work required from my side and request me to provide a quotation. After PC&E engaged China Status, Gordon would assign one of his staff, usually a foreman, to handle communications and any follow-up with my side.
